claims.text: No official assessment of FLIR1 has been published by AARO, unlike GO FAST, Aguadilla and Mt Etna. Reasoning: AARO's 19 Nov 2024 SASC case slides cover the latter three and not FLIR1; absence from a public case-slide deck is not proof no assessment exists, but it is the state of the public record.

claims.text: AARO assessed GO FAST as an object at approximately 13,000 feet travelling around 45 mph with 60-knot winds; it 'did not demonstrate any anomalous speeds or flight characteristics.'

claims.text: GO FAST (January 2015, off Florida's east coast): AARO assessed the object at approximately 13,000 feet travelling about 45 mph with 60-knot winds, concluding it 'did not demonstrate any anomalous speeds or flight characteristics.'

edges.note: GO FAST is the video Gallaudet says was attached to the recalled Fleet Forces Command safety message, and the one AARO later reanalysed on parallax grounds.

edges.label: AARO parallax reanalysis: no anomalous speed or flight characteristics
edges.note: AARO's SASC case slides place the object at roughly 13,000 feet at about 45 mph with 60-knot winds. The analysis addresses apparent speed; it does not address the recall of the fleet safety message built on the same footage.

edges.label: AARO's case work does not address the domestic incursion wave
edges.note: Neither the published case slides nor the FY2025 report present an assessment of the Langley, New Jersey or Barksdale incursions, which are handled as a counter-UAS force-protection matter by NORTHCOM and JIATF-401 instead. Reasoning: absence across all published AARO products, not a stated jurisdictional ruling.
